title: Define an ancestry-matched cohort

blocks.what_we_do: Apply a rule, fixed in advance, to the first four projected PCs. The rule flags samples that are more than six standard deviations from the European reference.
blocks.why:
In this teaching design, the main analysis uses a cohort that broadly matches the European reference. The rule has three parts. First, take the European reference samples. For each of PC1 to PC4, calculate their mean and their [standard deviation](docs/glossary.md#standard-deviation) (a measure of how spread out the values are). Second, convert each study score into a distance from that mean, counted in standard deviations. Third, flag a sample as an [outlier](docs/glossary.md#outlier) if its largest distance, ignoring the sign, is above six.

This is a rule for this study only. It is not a general way to classify ancestry. Apply it before you look at any association results, and report who was excluded.
blocks.you_need: The reference and study scores from step 5.4, and the reference labels used in step 5.5.
blocks.command:
```{r s5-6}
ref <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.4", "ref_scores"), ".sscore"))
study <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.4", "study_scores"), ".sscore"))
metadata <- guided_table(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "pca_reference", "ref1000g_grch38.psam"))
eur <- metadata$SuperPop[match(ref$IID, metadata$IID)] == "EUR"
columns <- paste0("PC", 1:4, "_AVG")
r <- sapply(ref[eur, columns, drop = FALSE], as.numeric)
s <- sapply(study[columns], as.numeric)
centre <- colMeans(r)
spread <- sqrt(colMeans(sweep(r, 2, centre, "-")^2))
z <- sweep(sweep(s, 2, centre, "-"), 2, spread, "/")
bad <- study$IID[apply(abs(z), 1, max) > 6]
remove <- guided_list(bad, guided_path(cfg, "5.6", "remove.txt"), TRUE)
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "4.6"), "--remove", remove, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "5.6")))
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "5.6", "4.6")
guided_register(cfg, "5.6", "5.4", 1811, 238513, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s4-6_state --remove results/guided/s5-6_remove.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s5-6_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

R applies the rule and writes the list of flagged sample IDs (IIDs). `--remove` takes out the samples on that list from the full study data. `--make-pgen` saves the retained cohort. `--pfile` reads the named genotype files in PLINK 2 format. `--out` sets the name of the output files. `--threads 2` limits the number of worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the working memory to 2048 MiB.
blocks.expected_result:
33 remaining outlier records are excluded. 1,811 samples and 238,513 variants remain. Some of the simulated outliers were already removed in earlier QC steps. So 33 is not the total number of outliers in the original data.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message and the previous step. Keep the command and the console log. Do not use files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: Large differences in ancestry compared with the reference, and possible technical outliers. A mismatch needs a review and a written study design. It does not mean that the excluded people are unsuitable in general.
blocks.quick_check:
Why does the rule use four PCs and not only the two shown in the plot?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

A difference that is weak or invisible on the first two axes can appear on later axes.

</details>
